newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN COURT REJECTS FRENCH RULING ON LOTTERY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN COURT REJECTS FRENCH RULING ON LOTTERY.

text.p: Bulgaria's administrative court on Wednesday rejected an appeal by Greek firm Intracom for it to accept a French ruling that the Bulgarian lottery should pay Intracom compensation for cancelling a contract.

Last September a Sofia court refused to legalise a decision of the International Arbitrage Court in Paris. The Paris court ruled in 1995 that the Bulgarian lottery should pay Intracom more than $6.5 million as compensation for cancelling a contract in 1993.

"The supreme administrative court rejected the appeal of the Greek firm Intracom in a case laid by it against Bulgaria's sports Totalisator and left in force a decision of Sofia's City Court from last September," state radio said.

Intracom and its daughter firm Intralot sealed a new 12-year deal with the sports lottery operator on September 16 and its managing director Pericles Katsioulas told Reuters in an interview that under the contract the Greek grouping would not implement the decision of the Paris Court.
The contract has sparked a row in Bulgaria amid fears that the Greek group would siphon off lottery profits.
Katsioulas denied all fears saying that under the contract Intracom would develop the lottery and sharply increase its profits by implementing modern automatic systems.
Bulgaria's chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said the contract should be invalid as it had not been signed by authorised officials.
